messages:
mike: heads-up — last 30m we've seen repeated ECC/Xid bursts on a subset of gpus in us-west-2. Alert fired, dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/GPUs/health?orgId=1

sre-bot: Alert: dcgm_ecc_errors_total > 0 (grouped by gpu_id) on node gpu-node-27 (us-west-2). Count: 7 in 10m. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/2332 :rotating_light:

anya: looking... saw a couple other nodes with 1-2 spikes each. Pattern: short bursts, then quiet. could be noisy ECC counters or transient firmware hiccups. :eyes:

samir: if these are short bursts we should avoid immediate automated drains, we've been losing capacity to false positives. prefer hysteresis or multi-window correlation first.

mike: agreed. current alert rule is basically dcgm_ecc_errors_total > 0 for 5m — too chatty. proposing we change to increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 3 OR increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m]) > 1, grouped by (node, gpu_id). then only page on cardinality > 1 per node or sustained over 2 windows.

anya: +1 to grouping. also add a recording rule to track recent_bursts_per_gpu = increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[1h]) so we can query trend without heavy eval. Example rule I sketched: ```yaml
- record: infra:gpu:ecc_bursts_1h:increase
  expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[1h])
```

samir: i like the recording rule. for alerting I propose: ```yaml
- alert: GPU_ECC_Burst_Sustained
  expr: (
    increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 3 or
    increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m]) > 1
  )
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained ECC/Xid bursts on {{ $labels.node }}/{{ $labels.gpu_id }}"
```

anya: also think about adding node-level suppression: only page if more than 1 gpu on same node fires within 15m, or if the GPU has >5 bursts in 1h. Prevents single noisy card from causing page for the whole node.

alex: ops/process question — if we relax sensitivity we may miss fast-degrading cards. Can we add a nightly sweep job that marks GPUs with persistent small bursts (e.g., bursts >=3 in 24h) into a "review" label and schedule a maintenance drain if they hit review 3 times in a week? That reduces noisy pages but keeps lifecycle for recurring flakes.

mike: yeah, that sounds sensible. propose two changes: 1) change alert rule to the hysteresis version above; 2) add a cron job (k8s CronJob) that queries the recording rule and writes annotations to our inventory (gpu-inventory service) with tag 'needs-review' when infra:gpu:ecc_bursts_1h >= 3. If a GPU receives 'needs-review' 3 times in 7d, create a jira and auto-schedule drain.

samir: can we make that CronJob idempotent + rate-limited and add a safelist for known noisy instances (old firmware) to avoid repeated churn? Also ensure region-aware behavior: don't auto-schedule drain in regions with <20% spare capacity.

anya: good call. I'll draft a prometheus rules PR and a k8s CronJob manifest. snippet for the query in the job: ```bash
curl -s "$PROM_URL/api/v1/query?query=infra:gpu:ecc_bursts_1h:increase%20%3E=%203" | jq .
```

mike: volunteer to review PR + run a canary rollout to us-west-2 staging. we'll keep page severity low (warning) initially and monitor tokenized impact on scheduling and oncall noise.

alex: please add a dashboard panel that shows flagged GPUs, times flagged, and node spare capacity so SRE can make replacement decisions quickly.

sre-bot: Note: created alert ticket #AI-3983 for the proposed change. Also scheduled a 2h monitoring window after deployment.

mike: timeline — PR by EOD tomorrow, canary deploy on thursday, monitoring window 24-48h. @samir @anya @alex can you be oncall for the rollout?

samir: I can.

anya: available.

alex: can do partial coverage.

mike: thanks. action items: anya -> PR with rule + recording rule; samir -> CronJob + safelist logic; alex -> dashboard panel and capacity check; mike -> review + canary deploy. We'll reconvene after the 24h window. :white_check_mark:
